A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDI research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across the appendix reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIA comparisons, CDI evaluations, feature ablations, robustness experiments, and appendix analyses on diffusion models trained on ImageNet and COCO.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds CLiD experiments, evaluations on additional model variants, and an analysis of unequal suspect and reference dataset sizes.

M1.justification: Appendix H.1 adds an evaluated CDI extension incorporating CLiD-derived features. The original feature definitions, logistic-regression scoring model, and Welch's t-test pipeline remain unchanged. The autoencoder reconstruction feature in Appendix G was already present in v1.

E1.justification: The original ImageNet/COCO coverage and image-generation tasks are retained. However, v3 Table 6 adds SiT, MDT, and DiMR evaluations without specifying their datasets or task settings, preventing a reliable judgment about additional data coverage. The text/audio extension in Appendix H.3 is discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds standalone CLiD results for seven conditional models in Appendix H.1, Table 4, explicitly comparing them with the existing MIA results. Denoising Loss, SecMIstat, PIA, and PIAN remain. CLiD is excluded from U-ViT256-Uncond and is not added to the existing dataset-inference ROC comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix M adds experiments varying |U|/|P| from 1.00 to 0.10, extending v1's equal-size setup. Table 6 also introduces five target-model configurations across SiT, MDT, and DiMR. These are additional settings; the original splits, five-fold scoring procedure, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Table 5 newly tests the contribution of CLiD features, while Appendix M and Table 9 test sensitivity to having fewer unpublished reference samples. This differs from the retained experiment mixing members and non-members within the suspect set. Existing feature, training-step, model-access, and SHAP analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 1,000 randomized trials, arithmetic averaging of p-values, and 95% confidence intervals for the corresponding plots. Existing uncertainty entries in the MIA tables are unchanged. The additions introduce no new run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original results remain unchanged, but Tables 4–6 and 9 add substantial quantitative evidence on CLiD, feature extension, additional models, and reference imbalance. Table 5 reports 30 required samples for CDI with CLiD versus 70 for base CDI on U-ViT256-T2I-Deep. Table 6 reports thresholds of 200–2,000 samples on the added models. These are new variant and setting results.

T1.justification: The diffusion losses, original feature equations, statistical hypotheses, and Cohen's d/power calculation are retained. The CLiD extension and imbalance study introduce no new formal derivation, theorem, proof, or revised mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: limitations of individual MIAs, CDI's feature aggregation and statistical testing, and identification with as few as 70 samples. The 30-sample result concerns the appendix's CLiD extension and does not replace the headline claim.

C2.justification: Appendix H interprets the CLiD results as evidence that CDI benefits from improved membership features, explains CLiD's incompatibility with the unconditional model, and discusses extension through latent-space features to other modalities. Appendix M newly argues that increasing the suspect set can mitigate reference-set imbalance. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: The original hyperparameters, model details, A100 resource disclosures, feature-extraction timings, and checkpoint-access information are retained in the relocated experimental-setup appendix. The repository link added to the abstract and broader-impact section already appeared in v1. The new experiments receive no expanded implementation instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds four cited works associated with CLiD, SiT, MDT, and DiMR and connects them to CDI's extension experiments in Appendix H. All original references remain, and the main related-work discussion and research positioning are largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. The appendices swap the MIA-pitfall and p-value-reporting sections, separate and reorder the former training-step/model-details subsections, and relocate existing discussions around new Appendices H and M. Smaller changes include acknowledgments, contact information, and wording edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4–6 and 9, renumbers retained tables, and rearranges or resizes existing appendix figures. The original plots and illustrations remain. Figure 1's caption is rewritten, including an unexplained attribution to previous work and an unfinished final phrase.

improvement.justification: The CLiD extension and reference-imbalance study strengthen evidence for CDI's adaptability and use when unpublished reference data are scarce; additional model evaluations provide further support. The gains are limited by sparse implementation details for the additions and Section 5's unreconciled statement that all experiments use equal suspect/reference sizes. Overall, v3 modestly strengthens the empirical case.
